intro: Adventure sports in India are often grouped the way the Ministry of Tourism groups them: land, water and air. Land sports range from a day hike to a Himalayan expedition; water sports from a calm kayak paddle to Grade IV rapids and scuba diving; air sports from a tandem paraglide to a skydive at 10,000 feet.

The list below covers every major adventure sport available in India, with a short explanation, the best places and seasons, and a link to our detailed guide where there is one. The comparison table at the end helps you choose by difficulty and season.
quickAnswer: Popular adventure sports in India include trekking, mountaineering, rock climbing, skiing, mountain biking and camping on land; river rafting, kayaking, scuba diving, snorkelling and surfing on water; and paragliding, bungee jumping, skydiving and hot air ballooning in the air. Top places include Rishikesh for rafting, Bir Billing for paragliding, Gulmarg for skiing, the Andamans for diving and Ladakh and Uttarakhand for trekking.
takeaways: Land: trekking, mountaineering, climbing, skiing, biking, camping, caving, ziplining and desert safaris.
Water: rafting, kayaking, diving, snorkelling, surfing and beach water sports.
Air: paragliding, bungee jumping, skydiving, parasailing and hot air ballooning.
Most activities have a clear season, and several pause during the monsoon.
Choose licensed operators; the Ministry of Tourism publishes safety guidelines for adventure activities.

items.name: Trekking
body: From one-day hill walks to high passes above 5,000 metres, across the Himalaya, the Western Ghats and the North East.

items.name: Mountaineering
body: Learned through month-long courses at government institutes, then trekking peaks and expeditions.

items.name: Rock climbing and bouldering
body: Granite bouldering at Hampi, sandstone at Badami and city crags near Bengaluru, Delhi and Pune.

items.name: Skiing and snowboarding
body: Gulmarg is India's main resort; Auli and Solang suit beginners when snow allows.

items.name: Mountain biking and cycle touring
body: Supported rides from Manali to Leh, downhill from Khardung La, and trail rides in the Western Ghats.

items.name: Motorcycle trips
body: High Himalayan rides in summer and coastal, ghat and desert rides in winter.

items.name: Camping
body: Fixed tent camps by rivers, lakes and dunes, and wild camps on treks.

items.name: Caving
body: Meghalaya has many of India's longest caves; show caves such as Belum and Borra in Andhra Pradesh are easier introductions.

items.name: Ziplining and flying fox
body: Harnessed rides along cables over valleys, forts and rivers, run at sites such as Neemrana Fort, Mohan Chatti near Rishikesh and Mawkdok valley in Meghalaya. Short and suitable for most ages within operators' limits.

items.name: ATV rides
body: Quad bike rides are offered on the dunes near Jaisalmer, in snow areas such as Solang and Gulmarg, and at some adventure parks. Rides are short; wear a helmet and ride only on marked tracks.

items.name: Desert safaris
body: Camel and jeep safaris and dune camps in the Thar, the salt desert of Kutch and the cold desert of Nubra.

facts.Season: October to March (Thar, Kutch); May to September (Nubra)

items.name: White-water rafting
body: Grade I to IV rafting on Himalayan and Western Ghats rivers.

image.alt: White-water rafting on the Ganga at Rishikesh
image.caption: Rafting at Rishikesh

items.name: Kayaking and stand-up paddling
body: Calm-water trips in mangroves, backwaters and lakes, and white-water courses at Rishikesh.

items.name: Scuba diving
body: Try dives and certification courses around India's islands and west coast.

items.name: Snorkelling and sea walks
body: Reef viewing from the surface, or walking on the seabed with an air-supplied helmet.

items.name: Surfing
body: Beginner-friendly surf towns on both coasts.

items.name: Beach water sports
body: Parasailing, jet skis and banana rides at beaches and lakes.

items.name: Paragliding
body: Tandem flights with licensed pilots, and courses for solo flying.

facts.Season: October to May; Himachal closed mid-July to mid-September

items.name: Bungee jumping
body: Fixed-platform jumps, the highest at about 83 metres near Rishikesh.

items.name: Skydiving
body: Tandem, static-line and AFF jumps at a few airfields, often in scheduled camps.

items.name: Hot air ballooning
body: Sunrise flights over Rajasthan and at festivals.

sections.heading: How to choose an adventure sport
list: Start from your dates: some sports have short seasons, such as skiing (January to March) and Ladakh rafting (June to August).
Be honest about fitness and fears; tandem and guided options let you try something without mastering it.
Think about who is coming: families need activities with clear age limits; groups do well with rafting and camping.
Combine a big activity with easy ones, such as a paraglide plus a village walk, so the trip is not all adrenaline.
Try one new sport per trip and learn it properly, rather than ticking off many quickly.

sections.heading: Safety rules and regulation
paras: Adventure sports in India are regulated by a mix of central guidelines, state rules and local orders. The Ministry of Tourism has published safety guidelines for adventure activities; states such as Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh license rafting and paragliding operators and suspend them during the monsoon; and district authorities close waterfalls, rivers and trails in dangerous conditions.

For travellers, the practical rules are simple: book licensed or registered operators, use certified guides and pilots, wear the safety equipment provided, respect seasonal closures, and be honest about your health.

safety: Choose licensed operators and trained, certified guides, instructors and pilots.
Wear helmets, life jackets and harnesses as instructed, for the entire activity.
Respect official seasonal closures, especially in the monsoon.
Declare medical conditions; many activities have health, age and weight limits.
Buy insurance that covers adventure sports and the altitude you will reach.

faqs.q: What are the most popular adventure sports in India?
faqs.a: Trekking, river rafting, paragliding, scuba diving, skiing, bungee jumping and camping.

faqs.q: Where can I do adventure sports in India?
faqs.a: Rishikesh for rafting and bungee, Bir Billing for paragliding, Gulmarg for skiing, the Andamans for diving, and Ladakh and Uttarakhand for treks and expeditions.

faqs.q: Which adventure sports can beginners try in India?
faqs.a: Tandem paragliding, short rafting stretches, snorkelling, sea walks, try dives, calm-water kayaking, easy treks and ziplining.

faqs.q: Are adventure sports in India regulated?
faqs.a: Yes. The Ministry of Tourism has published safety guidelines, several states license operators, and local authorities impose seasonal closures.

faqs.q: What adventure sports are there in India in winter?
faqs.a: Skiing, snow treks, desert safaris, diving, snorkelling and surfing on the coasts, and hot air ballooning in Rajasthan.

faqs.q: Where can I try ziplining in India?
faqs.a: At sites such as Neemrana Fort in Rajasthan, Mohan Chatti near Rishikesh and Mawkdok valley in Meghalaya.
